title: Split-phase, wye and delta systems
source: Written for ELECT 212 Labs 4-6 (120/240 V single-phase three-wire, three-phase wye and delta).

cards.front: How is a 120/240 V single-phase three-wire system made?
cards.back: A transformer secondary with a grounded center tap. The center tap is the neutral; each end is a hot line.

cards.front: Why is it 240 V between the two lines of a split-phase system?
cards.back: Each line is 120 V to neutral and the two are 180° apart, so they add to 240 V.

cards.front: Which loads connect line to neutral, and which line to line?
cards.back: 120 V loads (receptacles, lighting) line to neutral. 240 V loads (ranges, dryers, water heaters, A/C) line to line.

cards.front: What current does the neutral of a split-phase system carry?
cards.back: The difference of the line currents: I_N = |I_L1 − I_L2|. Balanced loads give 0 A.

cards.front: Worked: 15 A on L1 and 9 A on L2. Neutral current?
What is a multiwire branch circuit?
cards.back: Two or more hots with a voltage between them sharing one neutral (NEC Article 100).

cards.front: What disconnect rule applies to a multiwire branch circuit?
cards.back: All the hots must open together: a 2-pole breaker or handle tie (NEC 210.4(B)).

cards.front: What happens when the neutral of a split-phase circuit opens?
cards.back: The 120 V loads on opposite lines end up in series across 240 V. The smaller load (higher resistance) gets most of the voltage.

cards.front: Worked: open neutral, 1000 W and 100 W 120 V lamps on opposite lines. Voltage on each?
cards.back: R = 14.4 Ω and 144 Ω; I = 240 ÷ 158.4 = 1.52 A. 1000 W lamp: about 22 V. 100 W lamp: about 218 V (burns out).

cards.front: Why must a shared neutral not depend on a receptacle for continuity?
cards.back: Removing the device would open the neutral for the other circuit and cause open-neutral voltages (NEC 300.13(B)).

cards.front: How far apart are the three voltages of a three-phase system?
What is phase sequence (rotation)?
cards.back: The order in which the phases peak, for example A-B-C.

cards.front: How do you reverse a three-phase motor?
cards.back: Swap any two of the three lines.

cards.front: Give three reasons three-phase power is used.
cards.back: Smooth, constant power delivery; more power per pound of copper; three-phase motors are simpler and self-starting.

cards.front: What is the difference between line values and phase values?
cards.back: Line values are measured between lines or in the line wires. Phase values are across (or through) one winding or one load.

cards.front: What is the square root of 3, and when does it appear?
cards.back: About 1.732. It appears when converting between line and phase values, and in the three-phase power formula using line values.

cards.front: In a wye, how do line and phase voltage compare?
cards.back: V_line = 1.732 × V_phase.

cards.front: In a wye, how do line and phase current compare?
cards.back: They are equal.

cards.front: Line-to-line voltage of a 120 V-per-phase wye?
Line-to-neutral voltage of a 480 V wye?
Why is a 120 V wye 208 V line to line instead of 240 V?
cards.back: The two phase voltages are 120° apart, not 180°, so their phasor difference is 1.732 × 120.

cards.front: What does the neutral carry on a balanced wye?
cards.back: 0 A. The three phase currents cancel.

cards.front: How do you find neutral current on an unbalanced resistive wye?
cards.back: I_N = √(Ia² + Ib² + Ic² − IaIb − IbIc − IcIa).

cards.front: Worked: unbalanced wye, 10 A, 8 A and 6 A. Neutral current?
Why can a wye neutral carry more current than the phases?
cards.back: Non-linear loads make triplen harmonics (3rd, 9th...) that add in the neutral instead of cancelling.

cards.front: In a delta, how do line and phase voltage compare?
cards.back: They are equal.

cards.front: In a delta, how do line and phase current compare?
cards.back: I_line = 1.732 × I_phase.

cards.front: Worked: 240 V delta, each load draws 10 A. Line current?
Does a plain 3-wire delta have a neutral?
cards.back: No.

cards.front: In a delta lab, where do you clamp to read phase amps versus line amps?
cards.back: Phase amps: around a load leg inside the delta. Line amps: around a feeder wire. Line amps are larger.

cards.front: What is a high-leg (wild-leg) delta?
cards.back: A 240 V delta with one winding center-tapped for a neutral, giving 120/240 V four-wire service.

cards.front: What voltage does the high leg read to neutral?
cards.back: About 208 V.

cards.front: How must the high leg be identified, and where does it go in a panel?
cards.back: Marked orange (NEC 110.15), and on the B phase in panelboards (NEC 408.3(E)).

cards.front: How much of three-transformer capacity can an open-delta bank carry?
Three-phase power formula using line values?
cards.back: P = 1.732 × V_line × I_line × PF.

cards.front: Three-phase power formula using phase values?
cards.back: P = 3 × V_phase × I_phase × PF.

cards.front: Worked: balanced 240 V delta heaters, 17.3 A per line, PF 1. Power?
A 240 V heater runs on 208 V. About how much heat does it give?
cards.back: About 75%: power varies with voltage squared, (208/240)² ≈ 0.75.

cards.front: What is apparent power in a three-phase circuit?
cards.back: S = 1.732 × V_line × I_line, in VA.

cards.front: Why can't you de-energize a multiwire circuit by turning off one breaker?
cards.back: The shared neutral still carries the other circuit's current.

cards.front: What is the danger of connecting a 120 V load on a high-leg delta?
cards.back: If it lands on the high leg it gets about 208 V.

cards.front: Why measure every voltage combination on an unfamiliar system?
cards.back: Delta systems (ungrounded, corner-grounded or high-leg) can give unexpected line-to-ground readings.

cards.front: What does an open neutral on a wye or split-phase service do to 120 V equipment?
cards.back: Applies unequal voltages, some near line-to-line, which destroys electronics and can start fires.
